image.alt: Parent, educator and toddler playing with colourful blocks together

items.body: A secure, responsive and joyful environment where babies and caregivers explore, connect and grow together: a gentle beginning to learning, bonding and discovery.

papers.title: Group 1
papers.subtitle: 8–12 months
papers.text: Responsive songs, stories, movement and shared play strengthen the parent–child bond and build security and trust. Crawling, reaching and grasping, sensory play with textures, sounds and water, early communication and a gentle first social experience.
papers.timing: Mon, Tue & Fri · 2 hours · 9:00–11:00 am or 4:00–6:00 pm

papers.title: Group 2
papers.subtitle: 13–18 months
papers.text: Toddlers grow from little explorers into active, independent participants, learning by moving, touching, repeating and experimenting rather than sitting still. Parents stay close as partners and a secure base.
papers.timing: Tue, Thu & Sat · 2 hours · 9:00–11:00 am or 4:00–6:00 pm · 15 children per batch

image.alt: Two children building a colourful block tower, with a note reading Let’s… I can do it. Let’s do it together.

items.body: A gentle bridge from home to school. Children enter without their mothers into a warm, safe and confident environment, and grow in independence and curiosity without being rushed into formal academics.

papers.title: Playgroup 1
papers.subtitle: 1.6–2.6 years · Early Exploration
papers.text: Play corners to touch, build and pretend; stories, rhymes and conversations; music, dance and movement; blocks, puzzles, sorting and matching for early maths ideas; painting and drawing; sand, water and dough; and small climbing structures outdoors.

papers.title: Playgroup 2
papers.subtitle: 2.6–3 years · Bridge Programme
papers.text: Children become more independent with belongings, handwashing, eating and tidying up; express themselves and learn new words; build friendships and take turns; fall in love with books; and discover early maths through counting, sorting and comparing real objects.

image.alt: Girl studying a plant through a magnifying glass, with a note reading I wonder why?

items.body: Ready for learning, not just worksheets, and without losing childhood. Children are gently introduced to the Super3 inquiry cycle of Create, Explore and Reflect, and learn that their ideas matter.

papers.title: Nursery
papers.subtitle: 3–4 years
papers.text: Inquiry through everyday play: wondering why a plant needs water, planning how to build a tall tower, testing what floats and sinks, or revisiting a drawing to talk about what they created.

image.alt: Boy investigating a tree stump outdoors

items.body: A year of intentional learning that fosters independence, critical thinking, confident communication and ownership of learning, through play, inquiry, stories, hands-on experiences and real-world interactions.

papers.title: LKG – K1
papers.subtitle: 4–5 years
points: Independence with belongings, routines and responsibilities
Communication: speaking, listening, vocabulary and conversation
Literacy foundations through Letterland phonics and storytelling
Maths through hands-on Singapore Math approaches
Young inquirers who question, predict and investigate

items.body: Children take charge of their ideas, make choices, solve problems and work together. Early years learning comes together through connected, life-based experiences rather than isolated subjects.

papers.title: UKG – K2
papers.subtitle: 5–6 years
points: Language & literacy: CVC words, blends, digraphs, sight words, sentence and paragraph writing
Mathematical thinking: number sense, reasoning, estimation and problem-solving
Understanding the world: nature, communities, materials and everyday phenomena
Creative development: art, music, movement, drama and construction
